title: Why have border control games become so popular?
author: Revolutionary_Fun574

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: is this inspired by "Zero Stress King: Idle Defense" I really enjoyed that game

replies.author: Revolutionary_Fun574
replies.body: Yeah, the idea was to make something people could just pick up and play to chill for a bit. My wife actually tried it, and she’s not really into video games, but she ended up loving it. She described it as “chill and you don’t really have to think too much”, which I think sums it up pretty well.

replies.author: barret232hxc
replies.body: it's so funny b/c on paper I would have thought this kind of game is boring, but when I tried one out I got exactly what you described. Just a chill game. Which is funny b/c it looks hectic but I guess that's the magic of this kind of game

replies.author: Revolutionary_Fun574
replies.body: At first glance, it might look like you’re just watching units kill enemies, which doesn’t sound particularly exciting. But there’s actually a little puzzle going on behind the scenes. You’re constantly figuring out which units to upgrade, how to manage your resources, and how to make everything work together as the difficulty ramps up. In a weird way, it’s a game about building a defence system rather than destroying enemies. And honestly, there’s something pretty relaxing about watching the whole thing come together.

replies.author: Revolutionary_Fun574
replies.body: Also this is only a demo version. I’ll release the full game this coming Saturday
